T.M.Purushothaman vs Food Inspector on 7 January, 2016

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44469480/
1
O R D E R

The first accused in C.C. No.1340 of 1999 on the files of the Court of the Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Cherthala has filed this Revision Petition challenging the concurrent finding of conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 2(ia)(m) and 7(i) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

entities.text: Judicial Magistrate of First Class, Cherthala
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard.
3.
The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:-
On 25.1.1999 at about 2.30 p.m., PW1, the Food Inspector of Cherthala Circle purchased 750 gram of peas dhall from the shop of the revision petitioner.
The third accused was the firm from which the food items were purchased by the first accused.
The second accused was the partner of the third accused.

After sampling as per rules,
one of the samples was sent to the public analyst for analysis.
Ext.P14 report of the public analyst would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for peas dhall and therefore, it was adulterated.
On the request of the accused, the second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis.

Ext.P17 report of the Central Food Laboratory would show that the sample did not conform to the standard prescribed for peas dhall under Item No.A.18.06.14 of Appendix B of the PFA Rules and therefore, it was adulterated.
4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW4 were examined and Exts. P1 to P29 were marked for the prosecution.
DW1 was examined and Ext.D1 was marked for the revision petitioner.

5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P17 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated.
The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument.

entities.text: Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A)
(ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act.

Therefore, Ext. P17 report of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra).

It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra)
that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal.

In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and T.M.Purushothaman vs Food Inspector on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44469480/
2 found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and accordingly, the Court acquitted the accused.

entities.text: T.M.Purushothaman vs Food Inspector on 7 January, 2016 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The matter was referred to a Division Bench and the Division Bench also affirmed the said decision, submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.

Even otherwise, in view of the decision in Pepsico India Holdings (supra), the conviction in this case cannot be sustained as no laboratory was notified and no validated method of analysis was specified as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

In the result, this Revision Petition stands allowed setting aside the conviction and sentence passed by the courts below under Sections 2(ia)(m) and 7(i) read with Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the revision petitioner is acquitted for the said offence.
The bail bond of the revision petitioner stands cancelled and he is set at liberty.

Sd/-
